messages:
noah: Quick usability note: when reviewers approve items in the eval scorecard, keyboard users report focus jumping to the next item unexpectedly. Feels like a focus trap and it's jarring.

anya: Repro: open eval run, keyboard through examples, hit approve on an example with comments open. Focus moves to top of list instead of staying near your current position.

design-bot: Accessibility check linked: https://redwood.link/a11y-1760001111 1 warnings about programmatic focus.

devon: Likely culprit: after state update we call listRef.focus() to keep visible selection; that ends up moving to first tabbable element. Minimal fix: avoid global focus() calls, instead use element.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) and set aria-selected on the approved item so SR users get context without a focus change.

noah: Nice. Can we also add a small confirmation toast with aria-live=polite saying "Approved" so SR users get feedback without forcing focus?

qa-bot: Add tests: keyboard-only navigation across approvals, ensure focus order is preserved, and toast announced politely. Auto-check: simulate approve and assert activeElement remains within expected vicinity.

anya: Microcopy nits: toast should be short: "Approved" and if multiple approvals in a burst: "3 items approved". Keep aria-live polite and debounce multiple messages.

devon: I'll open a tiny PR: replace focus() with scrollIntoView + aria-selected updates, add polite live region and debounce for bursts. Gate behind ff_focus_fix_approve. ETA: tomorrow AM.

noah: Ship plan: behind flag, smoke tests in staging, enable 5% hosted, monitor keyboard a11y telemetry and support mentions. If anything breaks, rollback.

anya: Thanks all 60; I'll update the design doc and add the keyboard acceptance criteria.
